title: THEY DID EVERYTHING THE LORD COMMANDED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You must stay at the entrance to the tent of meeting day and night for seven days and do what the LORD requires, so you will not die; for that is what I have been commanded.' So Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD commanded through Moses." - Lev 8:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes on a note of complete obedience: they did everything the LORD commanded.

It is a good ending. And it is worth pausing over, because we know what comes next. The very first act of Aaron's sons in the following chapters ends in disaster (Lev 10:1-2). Nadab and Abihu will offer unauthorised fire and die before the LORD.

So this closing verse is not sentimental. It is an honest record of a day when they got it right, standing just before a day when two of them got it catastrophically wrong.

That is realistic about the Christian life. Obedience yesterday does not guarantee obedience tomorrow. A good beginning is not a finished race.

Paul, near the end, wrote: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith (2 Tim 4:7). Notice he said it at the end, not the start. And he had earlier admitted his own concern: I strike a blow to my body and make it my slave so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified (1 Cor 9:27).

Do not be complacent because things are going well. And do not despair when they have not been. Today's obedience is today's, and it matters.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I resting on past faithfulness rather than obeying today?
2. What is the one thing God is asking of me right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for grace to obey today. Keep me humble and dependent, so that I finish well and not only begin well. Amen.
